answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence expensive by requiring each account to lock a stake before its task claims count toward reputation. A verifier samples completed work, and proven fraud burns the stake while honest delivery releases it. Splitting one operator into a raven, opal, and forge of accounts does not multiply voting weight: each claim remains capped by the value at risk. The attacker must therefore tie up real capital in every sybil and lose it when caught, rather than minting influence for free.
